title: Making the github app more extensible?

nodes.body:
Short answer: yes, but I would split this into two layers:

1. Keep the hosted GitHub App server as a trusted control plane by default.
2. Make the repo-local agent runtime more extensible for actual question answering, coding, review, and custom skills.

Today, question answering is already handled by the GitHub Actions side, not the App server: mentions on issues/PRs/discussions enter [`agent-entrypoint.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-entrypoint.yml#L7-L21), route through [`agent-router.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L100-L241), and the `answer` job runs the agent and posts back inline ([router answer path](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L270-L365)). The hosted App/OIDC path is currently just auth brokerage: exchange GitHub Actions OIDC for a short-lived App installation token ([setup docs](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/deployment/setup-guide.md#L30-L45), [auth action](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-github-auth/action.yml#L58-L65)).

I would be cautious about moving answer execution into the App server first. The repo-local workflow currently gives each repository control over model credentials, runner environment, memory/rubrics branches, audit logs, workflow permissions, and PR review gates. A hosted answer server would need new answers for multi-tenant model credentials, data retention, memory isolation, rate limits, repo checkout access, tool permissions, and failure recovery.

A good implementation path would be:

1. Define an explicit hosted App boundary: auth broker only, webhook router, workflow dispatcher, or full hosted executor.
2. Start with “hosted dispatcher” extensibility: App server receives GitHub webhooks, validates installation/policy, then dispatches the existing repo workflows instead of executing the agent itself.
3. Keep `answer`, `skill`, `implement`, `review`, `fix-pr`, and `orchestrate` as repo-owned route contracts. Existing explicit routes and labels already map to this pattern ([supported routes](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/architecture/supported-workflows.md#L207-L231)).
4. Add a typed extension registry for routes/capabilities so new App-side triggers can target existing workflow contracts without hardcoding every behavior into the server.
5. Only after that, consider an opt-in “hosted execution” mode for lightweight `/answer` requests, with clear repository settings for provider credentials, memory access, permissions, and logging.

So: yes, making the GitHub App more extensible makes sense. I would not start by having it directly answer questions. I’d first make it an extensible dispatch/control plane over the existing repo-local runtime, then add hosted execution as an explicit opt-in mode once the security and state model is clear.

@sepo-agent /answer 

The problem is that it's slow: right now answer will take a bit since the agent needs to set up the runtime etc. how to handle this?

Yes, this is the right pressure point. `/answer` is “inline” in product behavior, but it is not lightweight operationally.

Current slow path:

- `agent-router.yml` first runs portal setup, including `setup-agent-runtime` before it can even run `extract-context.js` ([router](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L154-L169)).
- `setup-agent-runtime` always does `npm ci` and `npm run build`, then may install Codex/Claude CLIs ([setup action](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/setup-agent-runtime/action.yml#L79-L120)).
- Then the separate `answer` job checks out again, resolves auth/provider again, sets up runtime again, runs the answer agent, and posts the response ([answer job](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L270-L365)).
- `run-agent-task` may also restore session state and mount memory/rubrics before invoking `.agent/dist/run.js` ([run action](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/run-agent-task/action.yml#L212-L335)).

For `/answer`, I would handle this in phases:

1. **Add a fast acknowledgement path first.**  
   The hosted GitHub App can immediately post or react with something like “Queued answer run…” from the webhook server, while the full repo-local workflow continues. This improves perceived latency without changing trust boundaries.

2. **Make the router portal lightweight.**  
   Today the portal bootstraps the whole runtime before context extraction. We should split the deterministic router CLIs (`extract-context`, `resolve-dispatch`, `post-response`, reactions) into a prebuilt/minimal runtime path so explicit `/answer` can validate and route without `npm ci`, `npm run build`, or provider CLI setup. Explicit `/answer` already skips model dispatch triage because `requested_route` is set ([dispatch gating](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L179-L205)), so the remaining waste is mostly runtime bootstrap.

3. **Avoid double setup for answer.**  
   Either merge the portal and answer execution for the `answer` route into one job, or pass a prepared runtime/artifact from portal to answer. Right now `/answer` pays setup once in `portal` and again in `answer`.

4. **Cache or preinstall runtime dependencies.**  
   On GitHub-hosted runners, add npm cache keyed by `.agent/package-lock.json`. For serious latency, prefer self-hosted runners with Node, `gh`, `jq`, Codex/Claude, and warm npm cache already present. The setup action already has a self-hosted branch that reuses preinstalled Node ([setup action](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/setup-agent-runtime/action.yml#L39-L70)).

5. **Add an opt-in “fast answer” mode later.**  
   The GitHub App server could answer simple questions directly, but I would make that explicit, e.g. `AGENT_FAST_ANSWER_MODE=hosted`. That mode needs clear decisions for model credentials, memory/rubrics access, repo checkout depth, audit logs, and data retention. Without that, it weakens the repo-owned execution model.

Recommended first implementation: optimize repo-local `/answer` before moving execution into the App server. Specifically: lightweight portal runtime, no double setup, npm caching, and optional self-hosted warm runners. Then add hosted fast-answer as an opt-in path once the security model is explicit.
